publisher noun

also publishers, publishing house, publishing, bookseller

modern

Traupman 169

ēditor, ēditōris m.

noun, third declension

a publisher

Traupman’s word (feminine ēditrīx), from ēdere, to bring out a book, which is classical (see launch). Classically ēditor is rare and late: one who gives games (Lewis & Short). The editor of a text or a paper is another word (see editor).

Other words

  • bibliopōla, bibliopōlae m. — a bookseller (who had copies made and sold them)

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 1.2.6; 9.11.2; Mart. 4.72 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. publisher: bibliopōlium, a publishing house; Traupman 164

    Greek βιβλιοπώλης. In Rome the bookseller had an author’s work copied and sold it,, and was what a publisher is now. Post-Augustan.

See also editor, launch, book, bookshop.

SourcesLewis & Short: editor · Lewis & Short: bibliopola
